verdict.rationale: Obsidian's documentation says the vault already consists of non-proprietary plain-text Markdown files stored locally, which you can edit with other tools and use to 'switch to another app easily'. A Markdown-links option exists for interoperability, and users corroborate that they own their files, which can outlive Obsidian itself. Because the data is already in an open format, leaving needs no export step at all. missing for 10: a documented whole-vault export or conversion path for non-Markdown artifacts (e.g., Canvas uses JSON .canvas files, flagged by a user as a move away from markdown), and evidence on how portable Obsidian-specific syntax (wikilinks, Bases views) is in other apps.
